A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAE-based investigation of SDXL Turbo. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite the changed title, substantial expansion, and relocation of earlier material.

before.justification: v2 reports original SAE reconstruction measurements, feature interventions, quantitative interpretability analyses, block ablations, and SDXL Turbo/PixArt experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds RIEBench comparisons, multi-step generalization measurements, spatial probes, and Flux interventions.

M1.justification: The SAE architecture and training loss remain, but v3 introduces an automatic editing procedure using grounded-SAM2 masks, source–target feature ranking, and category-specific feature transfer and subtraction (Section 4.1 and Appendix E). Appendix B also introduces Flux interventions that inject learned features into every layer from layer 18 onward.

E1.justification: RIEBench adds paired source–target editing with nine explicit objectives, including object addition/deletion, pose, color, material, background, and style changes. This substantially extends v2's generation and feature-visualization evaluations. v3 also uses LAION-5B prompts for Flux training while retaining the LAION-COCO and texture-image evaluations.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates neuron and activation-steering baselines on RIEBench. Its Table 1 also adds neuron comparisons for all four blocks and PCA variants for down.2.1. v2's corresponding specificity comparison contained only random-image and same-prompt references; its texture baseline is retained.

E3.justification: The new main experiments use four-step SDXL Turbo and k=160 SAEs, whereas v2's main analysis used one-step generation and k=10. v3 expands hyperparameter sweeps and introduces curated masked image pairs, LPIPS/CLIP evaluation, and feature-count/intervention-strength controls. It also adds SDXL/Flux configurations and removes the PixArt extension.

E4.justification: v3 expands sparsity/dictionary-size analyses, measures reconstruction and feature overlap across denoising steps, and tests restricted intervention windows (Figures 2–3 and Appendix D). It adds spatial-position probes and editing failure cases. Earlier block ablations and random-feature analyses are largely retained, while the PixArt case study is removed.

E5.justification: v3 adds error bars and shaded bands to the multi-step curves in Figure 3, although their statistical meaning is unspecified. The earlier feature-level mean/standard-deviation convention and approximate confidence-interval formula remain in Appendix H. No increase in independent repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds editing-comparison results, transfer curves, Flux examples, and spatial-probe accuracies, and removes PixArt outcomes. Table 1 changes down.2.1 specificity from 0.71 (0.11) to 0.76 (0.10), and the random baseline from 0.50 (0.10) to 0.57 (0.09), without sufficiently explaining comparability of these revisions. Locality and reconstruction-table values are retained.

T1.justification: v3 formally defines a normalized source–target coefficient-difference score for feature selection in Equation 9. The existing SAE decomposition, TopK objectives, and superposition mathematics are retained; there is no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v3 adds RIEBench and finer-grained editing relative to neurons/steering as central contributions. It also adds cross-model generalization to SDXL and applicability to Flux, while elevating the four-step transfer observation already present in v2. The original causal-interpretability and block-specialization claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets temporal feature stability and block-dependent intervention windows, and discusses unexpectedly low down.2.1 participation in RIEBench despite its qualitative impact. It adds object-deletion and style-editing failure qualifications. Conversely, v2's discussion of weak causal effects in PixArt is removed.

D1.justification: v3 documents Flux training details, including layer 18, one million prompts, 10% activation sampling, 12,288 features, and k=20, plus benchmark aggregation/intervention rules and hosted SAEPaint instructions. The explicit experiment-code repository link in v2 disappears. Appendix E conflicts with Figures 29–32 about masks and preservation of spatial information, limiting reproducibility.

R1.justification: v3 adds supporting citations including SAeUron, Direct Inversion/PIEBench, Grounded SAM, Flux, and activation steering, and removes the PixArt-delta reference. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against earlier interpretability and layer-specialization research remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and its main narrative reorganized around generalization and RIEBench. Earlier qualitative and quantitative block analyses largely move into Appendices F–H, contributions are restructured, and the qualitative discussion is expanded. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v3 changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, expands Figure 1 across models, adds scaling/generalization plots and editing-comparison displays, and restructures Table 1 with comparator rows. Numerous earlier figures are relocated, while new Flux and intervention-window galleries replace the PixArt display.

improvement.justification: Direct neuron/PCA/steering comparisons and task-based editing evaluations address v2's limited comparison with alternative representations. Quantified temporal generalization and cross-model demonstrations also substantially strengthen evidence beyond its four-step illustration. Conflicting benchmark mask instructions and removal of the negative PixArt study weaken reproducibility and balance, but the overall improvement in empirical validation is substantial.
